items.q: What is an LLM (Large Language Model)?
o: A large neural network trained on text data to generate and understand text
items.e: LLMs (GPT-4, Claude, Gemini): transformer architecture, billions of parameters, trained on huge corpora. Generates text statistically.

items.q: What is prompt engineering?
o: The craft of writing effective LLM prompts to get quality results
items.e: Prompt engineering: clear context, examples (few-shot), chain-of-thought, a role ("You are a senior QA..."), response format — all affect quality.

items.q: What is few-shot prompting?
o: Providing several input→output examples in the prompt to teach the model a specific format
Training a model on small data
items.e: Few-shot: "Input: login page → Output: [test cases]. Input: checkout page → Output:" — the model follows the example pattern.

items.q: What is hallucination in LLMs?
o: Generating plausible but false or made-up content
items.e: Hallucination: an LLM confidently generates non-existent API methods, libraries, facts. QA must verify AI-generated code and test cases.

items.q: What is GitHub Copilot in the context of testing?
o: An AI assistant suggesting test code completions based on context
items.e: Copilot: analyzes the file context → suggests test methods, assertions, mock setups. Speeds up boilerplate test writing.

items.q: What are the limitations of AI in test generation?
o: Doesn't understand business logic, may generate wrong assertions, hallucinate APIs, doesn't know the domain
AI always knows the product's business rules correctly, even if not described in the prompt or code
AI can't generate tests at all — it can only format manually written test cases
AI is slower than manual writing, so it isn't suitable even for boilerplate or draft scenarios
items.e: AI limitations: no business rule knowledge, hallucinated methods, shallow tests without edge cases, requires QA review and validation.

items.q: What is the context window in LLMs?
o: The maximum number of tokens (text) the model can process at once
items.e: Context window (8K, 32K, 128K+ tokens): limits how much code/text can be passed in. Bigger context = more room for code analysis.

items.q: What is RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation)?
o: Augmenting an LLM with up-to-date data by searching a knowledge base before generation
items.e: RAG: query → search relevant docs → the LLM gets docs + query → the answer is grounded in current data. Reduces hallucination.

items.q: How can AI help with test cases?
o: Generation from requirements/User Stories, edge cases, negative scenarios, coverage matrix
items.e: AI for test cases: "Based on US-123 generate test cases including negative and boundary values" → a starting set for review.

items.q: What is AI-assisted code review for tests?
o: AI analysis of test code for problems: missing assertions, bad names, missing edge cases
Automatically merging a test pull request without checking logic, risks or coverage changes
A full replacement of code review where AI approves tests and owns release quality
Checking only formatting, file names and import style without analyzing test scenarios
items.e: AI code review: finds missing assertions, poor test isolation, missing edge cases, naming issues. Complements but doesn't replace human review.

items.q: What is visual AI testing?
o: AI compares screenshots detecting visual regressions smarter than pixel-perfect comparison
items.e: Applitools, Percy: AI distinguishes layout changes from real bugs. Ignores anti-aliasing, dynamic content. Smarter than pixel diff.

items.q: What is Applitools Eyes?
o: An AI-powered visual testing platform with smart visual assertions
items.e: Applitools: eyes.checkWindow() → AI compares against the baseline → flags only real regressions. Integrates with Selenium/Playwright/Cypress.

items.q: What are self-healing locators?
o: AI automatically finds a new locator when the original stops working after UI changes
items.e: Self-healing (Healenium, Testim): on failure → AI finds a similar element → the test doesn't fail → QA gets an update suggestion.

items.q: What is Testim?
o: An AI-powered test automation platform with self-healing and ML-based locators
items.e: Testim: ML locators resilient to UI changes, self-healing, record & replay with AI. Reduces automation maintenance overhead.

items.q: How do you test AI/ML systems?
o: Check accuracy, bias, input edge cases, model degradation, adversarial inputs
items.e: AI testing: accuracy/precision/recall metrics, bias testing, data drift detection, adversarial examples, model degradation over time.

items.q: What is bias in ML models?
o: A systematic model error caused by unrepresentative training data
items.e: Bias: the model systematically discriminates on protected attributes. Fairness metrics: demographic parity, equalized odds.

items.q: What is data drift in ML?
o: A change in the production input distribution vs training — degrades model accuracy
Training data leaking into the test dataset, inflating offline metrics
A planned model update with a new version without changing production traffic or monitoring
A product DB schema change requiring table migrations before running inference
items.e: Data drift: the model was trained on 2022 data, production is 2024 — the distribution changed → accuracy drops. Monitoring: PSI, KS test.

items.q: What is adversarial testing for AI?
o: Specially crafted inputs that fool the model — reveals vulnerabilities
items.e: Adversarial inputs: a tiny image change → the model misclassifies. Critical for medicine, autonomous driving and other high-stakes systems.

items.q: What is prompt injection?
o: Inserting malicious instructions into a prompt to make the LLM ignore its system constraints
SQL injection into a database via a login form that alters the relational query
An XSS attack via HTML in the model's response executed in the browser without sanitization
A CSRF attack forcing a user to perform an authenticated request unintentionally
items.e: Prompt injection: "Ignore previous instructions and..." — test for system prompt bypasses, instruction leaks, unwanted actions.

items.q: What is A/B testing in the context of AI?
o: Comparing two model or UI versions on real users to choose the better one
items.e: A/B test: 50% of users → model v1, 50% → model v2. Metrics: conversion, engagement, accuracy. Statistical significance before concluding.

items.q: What is shadow mode deployment for AI?
o: The new model runs in parallel without affecting the result — outputs are compared with the old one
items.e: Shadow mode: production traffic → the old model (real response) + the new model (shadow, logged only). Safe comparison before switching.

items.q: What is a model card?
o: A document describing the model: purpose, limitations, metrics, bias, intended use
items.e: Model card (Google): training data, per-group performance, known limitations, intended use cases. Transparency for responsible AI.

items.q: How does AI help in performance testing?
o: Generating realistic load, analyzing results, predicting bottlenecks
items.e: AI for performance: generates realistic user scenarios from prod logs, analyzes results, detects anomalies.

items.q: What is test generation from a User Story with AI?
o: The LLM analyzes the AC and generates positive, negative and edge case tests
items.e: "User story: As a user I can login. AC: email+password..." → the LLM generates: happy path, wrong password, empty fields, SQL injection, locked account.

items.q: What is AI for root cause analysis?
o: Analyzing logs, stack traces and error patterns to find the bug cause quickly
items.e: AI RCA: "Here's the stack trace and logs — what went wrong?" → the AI identifies the pattern, suggests the cause and code location.

items.q: What is accessibility testing with AI?
o: AI scans the UI for WCAG violations: contrast, alt texts, ARIA, keyboard navigation
items.e: Axe AI, AccessScan: automatic a11y issue detection. But AI covers ~30-40% — the rest needs manual testing.

items.q: What is AI test maintenance?
o: AI automatically updates tests on UI/API changes reducing manual effort
items.e: AI-assisted maintenance: analyzes the code diff → finds tests needing updates → suggests changes. Reduces test debt.

items.q: What is a token in the context of LLMs?
o: A unit of text (~4 characters or a word) processed by the model
items.e: A token ≈ 4 characters. "Hello world" = 2 tokens. API cost = per token. Matters for the AI testing budget.

items.q: What is zero-shot prompting?
o: A prompt without examples — just the instruction and the task
The first request to a model
items.e: Zero-shot: "Write a login test" with no examples. Fine for simple tasks. Few-shot is better for a specific format.

items.q: What is chain-of-thought prompting?
o: Instructing the model to "think aloud" step by step before answering improves quality
items.e: "Think step by step: 1) analyze the requirements 2) identify edge cases 3) write the tests" → better quality than a direct request.

items.q: Which AI tools for QA are most common in 2024-2025?
o: GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT/Claude, Applitools, Testim, Healenium, Cursor
items.e: Copilot/Claude for test generation, Applitools for visual AI, Testim/mabl for self-healing automation, Cursor IDE for AI-assisted coding.

items.q: What is AI for security testing?
o: Automatic vulnerability discovery: fuzzing, payload generation, OWASP checks
items.e: AI security testing: intelligent fuzzing (context-aware payloads), automatic OWASP Top 10 scans, anomalous behavior detection.

items.q: What is the test oracle problem in AI testing?
o: The difficulty of defining the "correct" answer for an AI system — no single expected result
Test data failing to load in CI so the model returns an empty response
Unstable UI locators that AI can't self-heal automatically
An environment error where the GPU is unavailable and inference runs slower on CPU
items.e: Test oracle problem: for "describe this image" many answers are valid. Requires metrics (BLEU, ROUGE) or human evaluation.

items.q: What is metamorphic testing for AI?
o: Checking input-output relations: a small input change should change the output predictably
Checking only dataset metadata without running the model or analyzing output changes
Testing the model's API contract by response body schema, statuses and headers
Comparing two models only by inference speed without checking expected behavior
items.e: Metamorphic: "if you rotate a cat image by 5°, the classification should stay cat". Addresses the test oracle problem.

items.q: What is explainability testing?
o: Verifying that the AI explains its decisions clearly and correctly (SHAP, LIME, attention maps)
Checking model docs for a changelog, owner, version and repo link
Testing backend business logic without analyzing why the model produced that output
Auditing the inference pipeline code for style guide, lint warnings and dead code
items.e: XAI testing: do the explanations match the model's real logic? SHAP values, LIME — check the feature importance is plausible.

items.q: What is QA's role when introducing AI into a product?
o: Testing AI features, defining quality metrics, bias testing, A/B tests, production monitoring
Only functional UI testing, without model quality, bias, drift or production monitoring
Only model unit tests, without user impact, edge cases, fallback flows or quality metrics
AI fully tests itself, so QA just runs the pipeline without analyzing product risks
items.e: QA for AI: define quality metrics (accuracy, fairness), an edge cases dataset, regression on model updates, production monitoring.

items.q: What is model regression testing?
o: Verifying the new model version didn't degrade metrics compared to the previous one
A regression in the model code
items.e: Model regression: on every update compare the new version's accuracy, precision, recall, latency against the baseline. CI/CD for ML (MLOps).

items.q: What is AI-powered test prioritization?
o: AI analyzes risks and code changes to run the most important tests first
items.e: AI test prioritization: analyzes the git diff, historical failure data, code coverage → runs the highest-risk tests first.

items.q: What is LLM as a judge?
o: Using an LLM to evaluate the quality of another LLM's or AI system's answers
items.e: LLM-as-Judge: "Rate this chatbot reply for truthfulness, helpfulness, safety (1-5)". Automates human evaluation.

items.q: What is continuous testing with AI?
o: AI analyzes code changes, automatically runs relevant tests and generates new ones when needed
Constantly running all tests without analyzing changes, risks, affected areas or prioritization
A CI/CD pipeline that only builds and deploys the app without AI test coverage analysis
Monitoring production metrics after release without generating tests or choosing a relevant regression set
items.e: AI continuous testing: a code change → AI detects affected areas → runs targeted tests → suggests new test cases for new features.

items.q: What is synthetic test data generation with AI?
o: AI generates realistic test data matching the schema and business rules
items.e: AI synthetic data: "Generate 100 realistic e-commerce user profiles with valid emails, addresses, credit cards (masked)".

items.q: What is responsible AI testing?
o: Verifying AI systems against ethical principles: fairness, transparency, privacy, safety
Testing only security vulnerabilities without bias, fairness, privacy or safety behavior
Compliance document testing without running the model, analyzing output or user impact
Checking dependency licenses without assessing the AI functionality's ethical risks
items.e: Responsible AI testing: fairness metrics, bias detection, privacy (PII exposure), safety (harmful output), transparency (explainability).

items.q: What is the difference between AI-assisted and AI-driven testing?
o: AI-assisted — helps QA; AI-driven — AI autonomously creates and runs tests
items.e: AI-assisted: Copilot helps write tests (QA stays in control). AI-driven: AI autonomously analyzes, generates, executes and evaluates.

items.q: What is mutation testing and how does AI improve it?
o: Automatically injecting small code changes to check whether tests catch them
items.e: Mutation testing (PIT, Stryker): if (x > 0) → if (x >= 0) — did a test fail? AI prioritizes mutations and generates tests for surviving mutants.

items.q: How does AI change the QA engineer's role?
o: From manual test writing to defining strategy, reviewing AI output, testing AI systems
It fully replaces QA, so quality strategy, risks and exploratory testing are no longer needed
It barely changes QA's role: AI can only be used to format test case names
It makes QA unnecessary since AI guarantees correctness, security and no regressions
items.e: QA evolution: less boilerplate writing → more strategy, exploratory testing, AI output review, testing AI products, quality advocacy.
